title: Define canonical SLI labels and automated error-budget reclaim workflow for model endpoints
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: We lack consistent SLI naming and measurement semantics across hosted, dedicated, and private endpoints. This causes confusion in dashboards, inconsistent alerting, and manual work when reclaiming or reallocating error budgets. Goal: Define a canonical taxonomy of SLI labels (latency quantiles, availability buckets, quality/semantic accuracy proxies), a standardized measurement window and tagging convention, and implement an automated error-budget reclaim workflow that can (a) surface candidates for reclaim, (b) run a safe preflight, and (c) execute reclaim actions (traffic steering, throttles, regional drainage) with audit logging.
acceptance_criteria: Documented SLI label taxonomy and examples for text-generation, chat, and embedding routes in the SRE confluence page
Instrumentation: telemetry emits canonical labels for >95% of requests in hosted and dedicated fleets
A prototype automation that detects sustained burn-rate >2x over 6 hours and creates a reclaim runbook entry in the console with suggested actions
Runbook: clear human-in-the-loop steps for automated reclaim to run in manual vs automatic mode
Post-action audit events (who/what/why) appear in the audit log and are visible in the Console rollout timeline
Unit/integration tests for SLI tag normalization and the reclaim orchestration state machine
Stakeholder sign-off from Platform PM (Priya Rao) and SRE lead (Daniel Park)
progress: 2026-02-19: Kickoff sync with SRE, Platform, and Metrics teams. Agreed to prioritize hosted + dedicated first, private later.
2026-02-24: Draft taxonomy v0.1 posted: latency.{p50,p95,p99}, availability.{success_rate}, quality.{semantic_similarity_topk}. Feedback requested in #sre-metrics.
2026-02-28: Metrics team prototype normalization middleware - emits 'sli_label' key; encountered 8% of routes missing model-version header (tracked as follow-up).
2026-03-04: Design review with PM/Console team: reclaim UI should expose human confirmation and a dry-run mode. Decision: default to manual mode; enable auto after pilot.
2026-03-10: POC automation detects burn-rate and opens a GitHub issue with recommended actions. POC repo: github.com/redwood-inference/slo-reclaim/pulls/12
2026-03-12: Integration tests for label normalization added in CI. Observability dashboard prototype at https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/slo-labels (internal preview).
decisions: Canonical SLI labels will be lower_snake_case and prefixed by domain: e.g., llm_latency.p95_ms, llm_availability.success_rate, llm_quality.token_overlap_k2
Measurement window: 10m rolling for alerts, 6h rolling for burn-rate automation decisions
Burn-rate thresholds: candidate reclaim when sustained burn > 2x for 6h and projected exhaustion within 72h at current burn

Reclaim actions ordered: 1) notify owner & propose cache tuning, 2) suggest increasing dedicated pool or throttling best-effort routes, 3) regional drainage to backup region, 4) model-variant fallback. Initial pilot will only create a runbook entry; auto-exec gated behind a safety flag
Audit and evidence: every reclaim action must produce a deterministic artifact (runbook entry + trace id + causal change request)
open_issues: Missing model-version header in ~8% of requests (metrics team ticket ENG-59321)
How to define 'quality' SLI across multimodal and few-shot prompts — feasibility research required
RBAC for automated reclaim actions in private deployments (legal/compliance review pending)

notes: Trade-offs: tighter automation reduces mean time to remediate but increases risk of customer-impacting actions without human oversight. Chosen approach biases toward visibility first.
This ticket intentionally focuses on taxonomy + workflow; separate follow-ups will implement model-fallback selectors and cost-optimization heuristics.
We will reuse existing rollout primitives rather than building a bespoke orchestration engine to reduce operational burden.
